title: Clear denominators of individual localized Tor classes
statement: Let A, B and C be commutative rings, φ : A → B a ring map, S a submonoid of B, and C an S-localization of B [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let N be an A-module and j ≥ 0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let f : B → C be the A-linear coefficient map given on elements by the localization structure map, using φ and (B → C) ∘ φ for scalar restriction. For every x in Tor^A_j(C,N), there are a unit u of C and a class y in Tor^A_j(B,N) such that Tor^A_j(mul_u,N)(x) = Tor^A_j(f,N)(y), where mul_u is the A-linear endomorphism of C induced by multiplication by u. There is no Tor-vanishing hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, localized derived-tensor homology identity in its proof; specialized to B in degree zero and expanded to clearing denominators of classes

proof.text: Choose a projective A-resolution P of N. Use the natural isomorphism Tor′ ≅ (Tor′).flip from lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry, then ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj for tensorRight. Naturality of the symmetry and ProjectiveResolution.leftDerived_app_eq give an identification of Tor_j(M,N) with H_j(P tensor_A M) commuting with every coefficient map M → M′.

For each module P_i, swap tensor factors and apply Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.rTensor to the localization map B → C. This is the tensor-localization compatibility of lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product (heterobasic rTensor form, tensoring over A while localizing the coefficient B). IsLocalizedModule.surj clears a denominator of each element, and IsLocalizedModule.exists_of_eq clears an element of the kernel. Swapping back expresses these equations using the coefficient multiplication maps.

Represent the homology class by a cycle v using surjectivity of homologyπ. Clear its denominator s to obtain z over B. Commutation of the coefficient map and multiplication maps with the differentials shows that dz lies in the kernel of localization. Clear this kernel element with a second denominator s′; then s′z is a cycle. The product s′s lies in S, and IsLocalization.map_units supplies its image as a unit u of C. Naturality of cyclesMap and homologyMap identifies multiplication by u on the original class with the image of the homology class of s′z. Transport the resulting equation through the coefficient-natural Tor computation isomorphisms, using injectivity of an isomorphism and its inverse identities.

lean.statement:
theorem tor_localization_denominators
    (A B C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    (φ : A →+* B) [Algebra B C] (S : Submonoid B) [IsLocalization S C]
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} A) (j : ℕ)
    (f : (restrictScalars φ).obj (of B B) ⟶
      (restrictScalars ((algebraMap B C).comp φ)).obj (of C C))
    (hf : ∀ b : B, f b = algebraMap B C b)
    (x : (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
      ((restrictScalars ((algebraMap B C).comp φ)).obj (of C C))).obj N)) :
    ∃ u : Cˣ, ∃ y : (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
      ((restrictScalars φ).obj (of B B))).obj N),
      (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).map
        ((restrictScalars ((algebraMap B C).comp φ)).map
          (u.mulLeftLinearEquiv C C).toModuleIso.hom)).app N) x =
        (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).map f).app N) y
